sections.title: Form and life cycle
sections.text: Common evening-primrose is native to North America and naturalised in many regions. It forms a rosette in its first year, then a flowering stem in the second year.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The basal leaves are about 10–30 × 2–5 cm; stem leaves are about 5–22 cm long. The flowers have four yellow petals. The elongated capsule opens into four valves and releases small seeds.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: University extension sources report eating young leaves and shoots. This entry does not assume food use for other parts or any medicinal effect.
